title.value: Mapping Parallelism in a Functional IR through Constraint Satisfaction: A Case Study on Convolution for Mobile GPUs
title.justification: The title directly reflects the paper's focus on mapping parallelism using a functional intermediate representation for mobile GPUs through constraint satisfaction.
title.quote: Mapping Parallelism in a Functional IR through Constraint Satisfaction: A Case Study on Convolution for Mobile GPUs

extractions.description: This paper explores the challenges of automatic parallel code generation for GPUs, particularly focusing on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on mobile GPUs. It presents a method for mapping parallelism using a functional intermediate representation (IR) and constraint satisfaction. The approach aims to automate the parallelization process, reduce memory usage, and improve performance. The paper evaluates its method using the VGG-16 CNN architecture on ARM Mali GPUs, comparing its performance with that of existing libraries and methods.

applications.quote: Using a convolutional neural network on a mobile GPU as a use case, this approach matches the performance of the ARM Compute Library GEMM convolution and the TVM-generated kernel consuming between 2× and 3.6× less memory.
